name: Game Boy (2 Players)
description: Two-player Game Boy link play, recreated in emulation by running two Game Boy instances connected by a virtual link cable. It covers games that originally needed two consoles, two cartridges and a cable. The hardware is the same as the Game Boy.

specs.sound: 4 channels (2 pulse, wave, noise), stereo through headphones

curiosities: On real hardware, link play needed two consoles, two copies of the game and a Game Link Cable.
Pokémon trading and battles between the Red and Blue versions used the link cable.
The Four Player Adapter (DMG-07) let up to four Game Boys link for games such as F-1 Race.
The Game Boy Pocket has a smaller link port than the original Game Boy, so linking the two needs a converter cable.
story: Gunpei Yokoi, creator of the Game & Watch, and his team at Nintendo R&D1 designed the Game Boy: four shades of green, a small Z80-like processor and four AA batteries for more than ten hours. It launched in April 1989.
From the start it had a link port: the Game Link Cable let two players race in F-1 Race, battle in Tetris and, from 1996, trade and fight Pokémon, which made the cable a playground essential.
With the Game Boy Color, it sold about 119 million units. Here two Game Boys run side by side, linked, as they were in the schoolyard.
